brief.title: Seed pitch for Tallyboard
brief.goal: Investors book a second meeting to see the pilot data.
brief.audience: Seed investors who have seen many scheduling tools and doubt the market size.
brief.bigIdea: Clinics lose a day a week to scheduling, and we give it back.

points.text: Front desks spend hours on phone scheduling
points.example: Pilot clinics logged 9 hours a week
No-shows fell from 18% to 7% in 3 clinics

brief.openingLine: Every Monday, Dana at Riverside Clinic spends four hours on the phone moving appointments.
brief.closingLine: Give us 30 minutes next week, and we will show you the pilot numbers clinic by clinic.

issues.problem: Investors doubt the market size, but no part of the brief states how many clinics need this or how big the market is.
issues.action: Add one line stating the total number of target clinics or the market size in dollars.

issues.problem: Point 2 proves a drop in no-shows, which is a different claim than the big idea about reclaiming lost scheduling time.
issues.action: Replace the no-show metric with a time-saved metric, or add a line linking fewer no-shows to hours saved.
